title: Venous cut-down
stem: Resus. A shocked trauma patient needs volume; peripheral cannulation has failed and IO is not available. Demonstrate a great saphenous vein cut-down at the ankle on the model.

phases.title: Cut-down
phases.goal: By hand: the great saphenous vein at the ankle, from landmark to running fluids.

review.text: Venous cut-down itself. Now that IO needles and ultrasound-guided lines are available, cut-down is rarely done in the ED; it is a fallback when those fail. Know the saphenous vein landmark (1–2 cm anterior and superior to the medial malleolus) and the steps.

notes:
Checked against ATLS (venous cut-down appendix) and standard procedural texts.

Nowadays IO access and ultrasound-guided peripheral or central lines are preferred; cut-down remains an option when these fail. Site: the great (long) saphenous vein, 1–2 cm anterior and superior to the medial malleolus (alternative: basilic vein at the elbow). Steps: aseptic prep, local anaesthetic if conscious, a transverse full-thickness skin incision (about 2.5 cm), blunt dissection with curved haemostats to isolate the vein (avoid the saphenous nerve), pass two ligatures under it, tie the distal ligature (leave long for traction), make a small transverse venotomy, dilate, insert the cannula or IV catheter and tie the proximal ligature around it, connect fluids, close the skin, dressing. Complications: infection, haematoma, phlebitis, nerve injury, arterial transection. Your notes list venous cut-down as a topic without detail.

steps.label: Saphenous cut-down
steps.hint: Landmark, prepare, transverse skin incision, blunt dissection, two ligatures, venotomy, cannula toward the heart, tie in, close.

opts.performHint: Do it with your hands. The vein and the nerve look alike in a hurry.
mark: Correct landmark for the great saphenous vein

qs.q: Preferred alternative when peripheral access fails in trauma?
Nerve at risk in ankle cut-down?
wrong: Posterior tibial nerve behind the malleolus

qs.q: Alternative cut-down site in the arm?
wrong: Cephalic vein at the shoulder only

qs.a: Injury proximal on the same limb
wrong: Shock with a low blood pressure

badge.name: Cut to the Chase
badge.flavor: Anterior to the medial malleolus, transverse, blunt, tie distal, cannulate, tie proximal.

cards.q: Great saphenous vein at the ankle lies…
options: On the dorsum of the 5th toe
For blood tests only, when veins are hidden
cards.why: IO and ultrasound are usually faster.
Stops back-bleeding; proximal secures the cannula.

cards.q: Saphenous vein cut-down is avoided if…
options: The patient is younger than 16 years old
cards.why: Fluid may leak at the injury.

options: Distal radius or ulna in every adult
Posterior iliac crest or the calcaneum
